newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON'S MCALLISTER NAMED IN SCOTLAND WORLD CUP SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON'S MCALLISTER NAMED IN SCOTLAND WORLD CUP SQUAD.

text.p: Brian McAllister became the latest international football graduate from Wimbledon's `Crazy Gang' on Thursday.
The uncapped defender was named in the senior Scotland squad for World Cup qualifiers against Latvia in Riga on October 5 and Estonia in Tallinn on October 9.
And manager Craig Brown, who has lost Everton's Duncan Ferguson up front, is convinced McAllister is worth his place.
"Brian may not be a household name north of the border, but he is a premier league player in England in a good Wimbledon side," said Brown.
"I have been following his progress for a number of years and hoped initially to involve him at under-21 level.
"Now we are taking him along with us as defensive cover because with two games in five days we need a larger squad than usual."
Glasgow-born McAllister, 25, joined Wimbledon as a teenager and helped them reach sixth place in the premier league on Monday, when Brown watched him in the 3-1 victory over Southampton.
Paul Lambert, of Borussia Dortmund, and Aberdeen's Billy Dodds were also given surprise call-ups in Brown's senior squad.
Lambert, who has two full caps, earns his recall after German international boss Berti Vogts kept Brown up to date on his form in the Bundesliga.
Dodds, with 14 goals the top scorer in British football this season, has never been capped at full level but wins his place as the in-form striker.
Scotland squad for the World Cup qualifying matches against Latvia in Riga on Saturday, October 5 and v Estonia in Tallinn on Wednesday, October 9:
Goalkeepers: Andy Goram (Rangers), Tommy Boyd (Celtic), Jim Leighton (Hibernian)
Defenders: Colin Calderwood (Tottenham), Colin Hendry (Blackburn), Brian McAllister (Wimbledon), Tosh McKinlay (Celtic)
Midfield: Craig Burley (Chelsea), John Collins (Monaco), Scot Gemmill (Nottingham Forest), Eoin Jess (Coventry), Jackie McNamara (Celtic), Gary McAllister (Coventry),

Forwards: Kevin Gallacher (Blackburn), Billy Dodds (Aberdeen), Gordon Durie (Rangers), Darren Jackson (Hibernian), Paul Lambert (Borussia Dortmund), Stuart McCall (Rangers), Ally McCoist (Rangers), Billy McKinlay (Blackburn), John Spencer (Chelsea), Nicky Walker (Aberdeen), Derek Whyte (Middlesbrough).
